Browser mode is an in-memory simulator. Start the TypeScript server to exercise the HTTP API and HMAC-signed demo grant.

What happens between tap and playback

Small, explicit checks. Fast failures. A trace you can explain.

DESIGN SKETCH
01 / RequestPlayback APIBounded JSON · input validation
02 / AccessEntitlementMember state · catalog rights
03 / PolicyProtectionRegion · device profile
04 / RouteEdge selectorLatency estimate · health fallback
05 / GrantSession tokenHMAC signature · short TTL

For a production system, replace the in-memory demo catalogs and counters with owned identity, rights, and telemetry services; use key rotation and a managed signing key; keep the player and license service boundaries explicit.

Security boundary

The API issues only a short-lived demo session grant after policy checks. There is no DRM license server, real playback URL, personal data, or production key material.

Reliability exercise

Inject a preferred-edge failure and follow the recovery path. The request keeps its access decision while the router picks another healthy edge and exposes the added latency.

API surface

Runnable TypeScript service. Node.js built-ins only.

LOCAL DEMO ENDPOINTS
GET/api/healthreadiness
POST/api/playback-sessionsdecision + trace
GET/api/metricsdemo counters
GET/api/eventsrecent events

Counters and catalogs live in process memory and reset on restart.

curl -s localhost:8080/api/playback-sessions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"member_id":"member-active","asset_id":"catalog-alpha","region":"us-west","drm":"Widevine","preferred_edge":"edge-west","latency_profile":"healthy","simulate_edge_failure":true}'

The same controls above can switch to the TypeScript API while running locally. Browser mode remains available as a no-setup walkthrough.
